newsitem.title: JAPAN: LME copper remains firm in quiet Asia trade.
newsitem.headline: LME copper remains firm in quiet Asia trade.

text.p: London Metal Exchange copper prices remained firm during quiet Asian trading hours on Wednesday, after bouncing in late inter-office trade overnight from Tuesday's lower close, traders said.

LME copper prices managed to hold above support levels during a test of the downside on Tuesday, although traders said the market was likely to continue probing lower after last Friday's rally to a nine-month high of $2,440 a tonne was followed by a sharp pull-back.
One trader said copper prices may have to slide as low as $2,270 a tonne before luring solid physical buying. He did not expect the Chinese would be looking to buy above $2,250/60.
The aluminium market remained buoyant, with Japanese noted among buyers on Tuesday when prices slipped toward $1,650 a tonne but showed no signs of breaking through that level, traders said.
At 0720 GMT, LME benchmark three-month copper was bid at $2,360 a tonne versus $2,359 at 1900 GMT on Tuesday, after rising in late inter-office trade from Tuesday's afternoon kerb close of $2,345.
Aluminium was bid at $1,680 a tonne, firming from $1,675 at Tuesday's afternoon kerb close.
